lesson.menu_title: The First 90 Days — Verbs That Govern Choices
lesson.menu_desc: Gerunds and infinitives for recommending and deciding -- 31 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- The First 90 Days: Verbs That Govern Choices
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Marcio Ferreira Santos | Lesson 9 -- The First 90 Days
phases: The Plan You Will Be Asked For

listenings.text: Welcome, and congratulations again. Let me tell you what we expect in the first ninety days, because people often get this wrong. We do not expect you to deliver a number. We expect you to understand the business. So I would recommend spending the first month in the stores, not in the office. After that, I suggest choosing one category and rebuilding the model there, end to end. Avoid announcing a big plan in week two. Everyone here has seen that before, and it never survives contact with the data. And please, do not try to fix everything at once. The people who succeed in this company are the ones who manage to finish one thing properly before they start the next.

This is the handover note from my side, before I leave the role. Three things I would tell my successor. First, we decided to price at category level three years ago, and I now think that was wrong. I stopped defending that decision about a year ago, but nobody changed it. Second, we keep collecting data that nobody uses. Somebody needs to decide what to delete. Third, and this is the one that matters, the team is good but it has learned to wait for permission. If you want them to move, you will have to say, out loud, that you expect them to decide without you. I regret not saying that earlier. Good luck.

extra_audio.text: First, the new director agrees to spend one month in the stores. Then he decides to rebuild the model in one category. After that, he avoids announcing a big plan too early. Next, he manages to finish the first category before the quarter ends. Finally, he recommends extending the model to the other categories.
